note: Hebrew anokhi ehyeh lakhem lerosh has no interrogative particle; it reads naturally as Jephthah's stated condition, though a question by tone alone is possible.

kjv: whomsoever the LORD our God shall drive out
mine: all that Yahweh our God has dispossessed
note: The verb horish is perfect, referring to the conquest already accomplished (v. 23), not a future driving out.

kjv: unto the plain of the vineyards
note: Abel keramim is a place name (Meadow of Vineyards); the KJV translates it as a common noun phrase.

kjv: and she (Jephthah's daughter) knew no man
mine: She (Jephthah's daughter) had never known a man
note: The circumstantial clause vehi lo yadah ish states her condition when the vow was carried out; the KJV wording lets it be read as her lifelong state after the vow, supporting the view that she was dedicated to celibacy rather than sacrificed.
Letannot is from tanah 'recount, retell' (cf. Judg 5:11), so the women went to tell or commemorate her story; 'lament' is a guess from context.
